method: Target = implied forward EPS x (1 + growth) x target P/E (or P/S or scenario blend where there are no earnings). Overweight if expected 12-month return (price upside + dividend yield) >= 8%, else Underweight. Each ticker carries its own 'as of' date. AI-generated opinion, not investment advice.

ABT.thesis: Q3 (Oct 21): adjusted EPS $1.42, comparable sales +7%, full-year EPS guidance reaffirmed. At ~18x forward EPS with a 2.4% yield, my model clears the hurdle even after trimming growth. Plans to spin off nutrition (~$8.5B sales) by end-2027.
ABT.risk: Sales guidance was cut on medical-device weakness and several analysts lowered targets (TD Cowen $118, Citi $122); Argus downgraded to Hold. Spin-off execution is a distraction. Stock is ~20% below its 52-week high.
ABT.basis: Fwd EPS $5.84 x 1.08 (1-yr growth +8%) x 18.5x target P/E; includes 2.4% dividend yield in return

ADBE.thesis: ~9x forward EPS and ~12% revenue growth look cheap, but the market is pricing AI-driven erosion of creative-software seats. My model lands just below the return hurdle.
ADBE.risk: Wells Fargo double-downgraded to Underweight ($225) and HSBC to Hold in mid-October; consensus is Hold. If AI tools commoditise the product, the low multiple is deserved. No new quarterly results since my last view.
ADBE.basis: Fwd EPS $26.85 x 1.05 (1-yr growth +5%) x 9.5x target P/E

ASTS.thesis: No earnings to anchor a multiple (TTM revenue $115M, net loss $619M), so the target is a scenario blend. Mixed news: Brazil spectrum approval and a Scotiabank upgrade (Outperform, $55.70) vs. Piper's downgrade on SpaceX competition. Refreshed from my Oct 15 view.
ASTS.risk: Binary outcomes: constellation build-out and carrier deals vs. dilution, competition and the pending class action (lead-plaintiff deadline Nov 13). Position sizing matters more than the rating here.
ASTS.basis: Scenario-weighted: 20% x $100 + 35% x $40 + 45% x $10 (about $38); no earnings anchor

BABA.thesis: ~12.6x forward EPS near the 52-week low, with TTM revenue up only ~4% and EPS down ~52% on investment in quick commerce. My model lands just under the hurdle; the consensus target ($186) looks far too optimistic to me.
BABA.risk: China tech sell-off (CSI 300 in a bear market), tightened e-commerce quality rules (stock fell ~6% around Oct 22), US blacklist issues (a judge granted a preliminary injunction on Pentagon-contract limits on Oct 27). Upside: cloud/AI re-rating.
BABA.basis: Fwd EPS $7.94 x 1.08 (1-yr growth +8%) x 12.5x target P/E

BKNG.thesis: ~13x forward EPS for a business with ~13% revenue growth and +56% TTM EPS; the stock is ~33% below its 52-week high. Q3 results land tomorrow (Nov 3), so this is a pre-earnings view.
BKNG.risk: Reported FTC action over hotel advertising and an EU probe on fake listings; AI-agent disintermediation fears hit travel stocks in early October; analysts have been cutting targets (Cantor $170, Wells $190).
BKNG.basis: Fwd EPS $11.13 x 1.12 (1-yr growth +12%) x 14x target P/E

CRM.thesis: ~15.6x forward EPS for an ~11% grower with expanding margins and large buybacks; Agentforce is the upside option. Management says the Braze deal doesn't change FY27 guidance.
CRM.risk: Acquisitions keep piling up (Braze ~$5.7B, Rune $375M); AI agents could compress per-seat revenue; Agentforce security flaws were disclosed.
CRM.basis: Fwd EPS $14.67 x 1.09 (1-yr growth +9%) x 16.5x target P/E

EXE.thesis: Largest U.S. gas producer: Q3 output 7.54 Bcfe/d, 2026 capex ~$3B, new CEO Danny Brown from Oct 26. At ~12x forward EPS, my model implies only low-single-digit upside, though consensus targets are far higher ($123).
EXE.risk: Earnings swing with natural-gas prices (TTM EPS is inflated by a one-time swing); several analysts trimmed targets in October. I could not verify how the stock reacted to Q3.
EXE.basis: Fwd EPS $7.79 x 1.05 (1-yr growth +5%) x 12x target P/E

ISRG.thesis: Q3 (Oct 20): EPS $3.00 vs $2.64 and revenue $3.05B (+22%) vs $2.91B; procedures +15%, gross-margin guide raised. Even at ~37x forward EPS, ~14% growth gives double-digit upside.
ISRG.risk: $450M antitrust-class-action settlement hit the stock after the report; tariffs and a high multiple leave little room for a growth miss; the stock is ~25% below its high.
ISRG.basis: Fwd EPS $12.07 x 1.14 (1-yr growth +14%) x 37x target P/E

LULU.thesis: Revenue growth is ~2% and EPS is shrinking, so I model slightly lower forward earnings and a modest multiple. The stock is down more than 50% from its high but consensus (Hold) target is only ~1% above the price.
LULU.risk: A 17% one-day drop on Sep 4 triggered securities-fraud investigations; Wolfe initiated at Underperform ($75); leadership reshuffle at Athleta. Upside: a cheap multiple if US trends stabilise.
LULU.basis: Fwd EPS $8.40 x 0.98 (1-yr growth -2%) x 11.5x target P/E

LVS.thesis: Q3 (Oct 21) missed: adjusted EPS $0.54 vs $0.68, revenue $3.22B vs $3.33B, on weak Singapore and Macau premium play. At ~12x forward EPS, a 3.3% yield and ~$950M of Q3 buybacks, the stock near its 52-week low offers upside if volumes recover.
LVS.risk: Targets were cut across the Street (e.g. Goldman $41, Wells $40, Jefferies $37); high-end Asian gaming demand is volatile and China policy risk is persistent.
LVS.basis: Fwd EPS $2.99 x 1.05 (1-yr growth +5%) x 12.5x target P/E; includes 3.3% dividend yield in return

MELI.thesis: Revenue +46% TTM and the stock is ~30% below its high after a ~14% drop on Oct 26 when Lula won Brazil's runoff. At ~40x forward EPS my model gives only a modest edge over the hurdle.
MELI.risk: Brazil political and currency risk, margin pressure from free shipping and credit growth (TTM EPS -9%). Citi upgraded to Buy on the dip. My price is from Oct 27 and Q3 results were not on the data page I used (it listed Nov 10), so check the live upside.
MELI.basis: Fwd EPS $42.21 x 1.22 (1-yr growth +22%) x 36x target P/E

META.thesis: Ad revenue is growing ~26% and TTM EPS +30%, yet the stock is ~21% below its 52-week high at ~18.7x forward EPS. That discount looks too large for a business compounding earnings at this rate.
META.risk: AI capex is huge (reported plans to raise ~$95B including a stock offering) and S&P moved its outlook to negative on Oct 30 citing negative free cash flow; legal costs from teen-addiction litigation. Secondary sources on Q3 details conflicted, so I rely on the price/multiple data.
META.basis: Fwd EPS $32.94 x 1.12 (1-yr growth +12%) x 20x target P/E

MSFT.thesis: Q1 FY27 (Oct 28): revenue about $92B (+19%) and Azure growth reported near 48%, with capex below what the market expected. ~25x forward EPS for double-digit growth leaves ~18% upside in my model.
MSFT.risk: Planned ~$25B bond sale (first in years) and a very large capex plan raise AI-return questions; stock slipped after earnings. Figures from secondary sources and not verified against Microsoft's release.
MSFT.basis: Fwd EPS $20.75 x 1.14 (1-yr growth +14%) x 26x target P/E

NFLX.thesis: Q3 (Oct 20) was uninspiring and the Q4 guide conservative; the stock fell to a two-year low, ~47% below its high. At ~17x forward EPS with ~15% revenue growth and +44% EPS growth, I think the reset is overdone.
NFLX.risk: Weak guidance, ad-tier and engagement concerns, and content costs; analysts cut targets after the report. Consensus target is $85.
NFLX.basis: Fwd EPS $3.59 x 1.15 (1-yr growth +15%) x 20x target P/E

NKE.thesis: Revenue is still shrinking (-1% TTM) and management expects another decline in fiscal 2027; at ~29x forward EPS the turnaround is priced in. My model implies a small decline.
NKE.risk: Upside from an earlier-than-expected recovery (Barclays raised to $45 Overweight); investor day Nov 16-17 is a catalyst; Wolfe initiated at Underperform ($28).
NKE.basis: Fwd EPS $1.29 x 1.15 (1-yr growth +15%) x 25x target P/E

NOW.thesis: Q3 (Oct 28): subscription revenue +20.5% (cc), margin 32.5%, AI net new ACV +65%, FCF margin guide raised to 36%. The stock then fell ~25% on slower Q4 cRPO guidance and AI-disruption fears; at ~23x forward EPS my model shows large upside.
NOW.risk: This is a falling knife: worst day on record, law-firm investigations announced, and sentiment on seat-based software is poor. Conviction is low because the multiple could keep compressing.
NOW.basis: Fwd EPS $4.54 x 1.20 (1-yr growth +20%) x 24x target P/E

NVO.thesis: ~12x forward EPS with a 3.2% yield and a DKK 15B buyback, but revenue growth has slowed to ~6% and Lilly keeps winning head-to-head obesity trials. My model lands just under the hurdle.
NVO.risk: Pricing pressure and Lilly's retatrutide data (Oct 28); CagriSema is the offsetting upside. Q3 results come Nov 4, which could move the stock either way.
NVO.basis: Fwd EPS $3.35 x 1.02 (1-yr growth +2%) x 12x target P/E; includes 3.2% dividend yield in return

ORCL.thesis: Investor Day set a FY30 revenue target of $225B+ and reaffirmed FY27 guidance (stock +11% on Oct 28, then -6% on Oct 30). At ~15x forward EPS my model shows ~20% upside if even part of the backlog converts.
ORCL.risk: Free cash flow is not expected to turn positive until the second half of fiscal 2028, funded by heavy debt; customer concentration in AI contracts; the stock is ~52% below its high.
ORCL.basis: Fwd EPS $8.53 x 1.15 (1-yr growth +15%) x 16x target P/E

OSCR.thesis: Revenue +43% and 2026 earnings guidance was raised at Investor Day; with the price off its high, my model clears the return hurdle. Refreshed from my Oct 15 view (price fell ~9%).
OSCR.risk: ACA marketplace subsidy/regulatory risk and medical-cost trend; consensus is Hold; Q3 results come Nov 5.
OSCR.basis: Fwd EPS $1.82 x 1.35 (1-yr growth +35%) x 15x target P/E

PEP.thesis: ~15.7x forward EPS with a 4.5% dividend yield, historically high for PepsiCo. Full-year guidance was cut, but that is in the price.
PEP.risk: Soda volumes are falling, KFC is switching to Coca-Cola in the U.S., and GLP-1 usage pressures snacks; several analysts cut targets (Citi $135, Piper $140).
PEP.basis: Fwd EPS $8.47 x 1.06 (1-yr growth +6%) x 16x target P/E; includes 4.46% dividend yield in return

PFE.thesis: 5.8% yield and ~10.8x forward EPS, but revenue is flat and I model no earnings growth. Total expected return (~4%) is below the hurdle; the price is already near its 52-week high.
PFE.risk: Patent-cliff exposure; positive pipeline news (ELREXFIO phase 3, TALZENNA label expansion) could surprise upward. Q3 results come Nov 3.
PFE.basis: Fwd EPS $2.76 x 1.00 (1-yr growth +0%) x 10.5x target P/E; includes 5.8% dividend yield in return

SE.thesis: Revenue +43% and EPS +33% with Shopee on track for ~$1B profit; the stock has fallen ~23% in two weeks to ~17x forward EPS. Refreshed from my Oct 15 view.
SE.risk: Margin concerns (DBS, New Street downgrades), a fintech-unit IPO idea that may dilute focus, and e-commerce competition. I couldn't verify the cause of the recent drop.
SE.basis: Fwd EPS $4.29 x 1.18 (1-yr growth +18%) x 17x target P/E

SPOT.thesis: Q3 (Oct 22): 306M premium subs (+9%), revenue +14% cc, FCF EUR 735M, and Q4 operating-income guide above consensus; the stock jumped ~8-10% to a 10-month high. At ~36x forward EPS, that is already largely in my target.
SPOT.risk: Family-plan crackdown could hurt user growth, music-label cost negotiations, and a high multiple. Consensus target $633.
SPOT.basis: Fwd EPS $15.96 x 1.20 (1-yr growth +20%) x 32x target P/E

TMDX.thesis: Revenue +26% TTM and 2026 guidance of $737-757M was reiterated; the stock is down ~55% from its high. My model clears the hurdle only narrowly, so the Nov 5 results matter.
TMDX.risk: Single-product concentration in organ transport, a law-firm investigation announced in September, and a CFO change. My earlier note about Oct 28 results was wrong: Q3 is reported Nov 5.
TMDX.basis: Fwd EPS $1.80 x 1.35 (1-yr growth +35%) x 32x target P/E

TTWO.thesis: The stock is driven by GTA VI (launch date reaffirmed as Nov 19, 2026). Analysts forecast EPS growing ~49% next year and the consensus target is $286, but I blend in a delay or soft-launch scenario.
TTWO.risk: Another delay would be a repeat of past drops; costs and dilution are heavy and GAAP earnings are currently negative. My price is from Oct 23; compare with the live quote.
TTWO.basis: Scenario-weighted: 25% x $290 + 50% x $235 + 25% x $150 (about $228) around the Nov 19 GTA VI launch

UBER.thesis: Stock is ~35% below its 52-week high; Q3 EBITDA guide is $2.86-2.96B and analysts see FY27 EPS up ~30%. At ~17x my forward EPS estimate, my model gives ~20% upside.
UBER.risk: EBIT missed estimates in four of the last five quarters, price reinvestment can absorb margin gains, a pending $14.8B Delivery Hero offer and $2.3B ezCater deal add debt and integration risk, and robotaxi disruption. Forward EPS here is my estimate (~$3.90), not a sourced figure.
UBER.basis: Fwd EPS $3.90 x 1.17 (1-yr growth +17%) x 17.5x target P/E

UNH.thesis: Q3 beat and 2026 guidance was raised; ~18x forward EPS with a 2.3% dividend. Earnings power is rebuilding.
UNH.risk: Medical-cost trend, a Texas AG investigation, and the stock is up ~24% this year so expectations are higher. Refreshed from my Oct 15 view.
UNH.basis: Fwd EPS $22.70 x 1.08 (1-yr growth +8%) x 18x target P/E; includes 2.28% dividend yield in return

WDAY.thesis: Revenue +13% and a 17x forward multiple, but the stock already trades at the consensus target ($209) after a ~90% rally from its low. My model lands below the hurdle.
WDAY.risk: KeyBanc downgraded to Sector Weight; $2.5B notes issued and AI-agent deals (Anthropic partnership, C1.ai acquisition) add execution and seat-compression questions.
WDAY.basis: Fwd EPS $12.07 x 1.12 (1-yr growth +12%) x 16x target P/E

WMT.thesis: High-quality compounder (revenue +6%, EPS +4%), but ~39.5x forward EPS is a very rich multiple for that growth; my model implies a slight decline in price terms.
WMT.risk: FTC data order on personalised pricing, tariff pressure on margins; upside from advertising and membership growth and an automation story. Q3 results come Nov 19.
WMT.basis: Fwd EPS $3.00 x 1.08 (1-yr growth +8%) x 36x target P/E; includes 0.8% dividend yield in return

ZETA.thesis: Revenue +36%, GAAP profit near breakeven, and a run of target raises (Goldman upgraded to Buy at $45, Roth $55). Refreshed from my Oct 15 view.
ZETA.risk: Thin GAAP earnings, a ~29x forward multiple, acquisition integration, and results on Nov 9.
ZETA.basis: Fwd EPS $1.08 x 1.30 (1-yr growth +30%) x 27.5x target P/E

IBIT.thesis: Spot bitcoin ETF. Bitcoin has no cash flows, so I have no valuation framework to justify an Overweight/Underweight call or a price target. Shown for completeness.
IBIT.risk: Highly volatile; bitcoin has traded around $80-85K recently, and fund inflows have been uneven since mid-July.
IBIT.basis: No reliable valuation anchor; no price target.

ETH.thesis: Grayscale Ethereum staking mini ETF. Same limitation as bitcoin: no earnings to anchor a target, so no rating. The fund is down ~40% over one year.
ETH.risk: Highly volatile; crypto legislation uncertainty (the Clarity Act failed a Senate procedural vote by 11 votes).
ETH.basis: No reliable valuation anchor; no price target.

AMZN.thesis: AWS is still growing on AI demand and TTM revenue is up ~15%, with ~$800B of sales. At ~24x forward EPS the stock is about 16% below its 52-week high after a Q3 miss.
AMZN.risk: Q3 fell short of expectations and the Q4 sales outlook was cautious; investors are worried about AI capex, free cash flow, and the up-to-$80B asset-backed borrowing. Note TTM EPS ($12.37) is inflated versus forward EPS (~$9.90).
AMZN.basis: Fwd EPS $9.91 x 1.15 (1-yr growth +15%) x 25x target P/E

APP.thesis: Revenue is up ~61% and EPS ~85% yet the stock trades at ~13x forward EPS, down ~70% from its 52-week high. If growth merely holds, the multiple looks too low.
APP.risk: I could not verify why the stock fell (down 10% on Oct 30); a securities class action is pending (lead-plaintiff deadline Nov 16) and nearly every analyst cut targets in October (UBS $790 to $414). Q3 results land Nov 4.
APP.basis: Fwd EPS $17.81 x 1.20 (1-yr growth +20%) x 14x target P/E

ASML.thesis: Monopoly in EUV lithography. Q3 net sales were EUR 11.7B (up from 9.3B) with a 57.5% gross margin; Q4 guidance is EUR 14.2-15.2B, and management says 2027-28 supply won't meet demand.
ASML.risk: Chip-cycle and AI-capex sentiment (the stock fell sharply in recent weeks), export restrictions on China, and my price is from Oct 27, before part of the post-earnings move, so check the live upside.
ASML.basis: Fwd EPS $64.85 x 1.22 (1-yr growth +22%) x 25x target P/E; includes 0.49% dividend yield in return

BIDU.thesis: Search/ad revenue is shrinking (TTM revenue -4%) and TTM EPS is negative, so I see no earnings catalyst. At ~15x forward EPS with low growth, my model implies roughly flat returns.
BIDU.risk: Upside case: AI cloud and the Apollo Go robotaxi business could be worth more than the market credits; I could not verify net cash or a sum-of-the-parts. Stock sits at its 52-week low and a class action is pending.
BIDU.basis: Fwd EPS $5.18 x 1.05 (1-yr growth +5%) x 14x target P/E

GOOGL.thesis: After the Q3 miss the stock fell ~13% in a day and is ~31% below its high, with revenue still growing ~22%. At ~20x forward EPS, I think the AI-search worry is partly priced in.
GOOGL.risk: Search revenue missed partly because AI Mode monetizes worse; estimates will likely fall further, and consensus targets ($406) predate the drop. A class action is pending. The 14.6x trailing P/E looks cheap only because TTM EPS includes one-time gains.
GOOGL.basis: Fwd EPS $13.82 x 1.10 (1-yr growth +10%) x 21x target P/E

HAWK.thesis: Recent IPO (May 2026 at ~$26) selling satellite radio-frequency data to governments; revenue is roughly doubling and adjusted EBITDA is positive. At ~5x forward sales the stock is down >50% from its IPO price.
HAWK.risk: Backlog slipped ($302.7M to $285M), growth is decelerating, and four analyst cuts in six months. A typical 180-day IPO lock-up would expire around Nov 3 (not verified). Share count is inferred from the quoted market cap, so the target is rough.
HAWK.basis: 12M-fwd sales $262M (TTM $168M x 1.56) x 5.5x P/S / 96.3M shares (no meaningful earnings)

HIMS.thesis: Revenue is up 28% to $2.6B and the stock trades at ~2.5x sales, down ~42% over the year. A recovery in margins plus steady growth gives modest upside.
HIMS.risk: TTM net loss (-$142M), an FTC lawsuit over subscription practices, a pending class action, and heavy dependence on weight-loss and men's-health launches. Earnings Nov 9.
HIMS.basis: 12M-fwd sales $3,148M (TTM $2,580M x 1.22) x 2.3x P/S / 233.4M shares (no meaningful earnings)

IONQ.thesis: Quantum-computing leader with revenue up ~370% to $246M, but at a ~$13B market cap that is ~52x sales with no earnings. My scenario blend lands slightly below the current price.
IONQ.risk: Dilution (a $2.0B equity offering just priced), acquisition integration (Elisity, up to $1.3B), large GAAP losses (-$1.36B TTM), and sector sentiment swings. Upside: DARPA QBI final stage, government funding.
IONQ.basis: Scenario-weighted: 20% x $65 + 35% x $30 + 45% x $12 (about $29); no earnings anchor

JD.thesis: ~7x forward EPS and a 52-week-low price; the market expects earnings to recover after the food-delivery investment drag (TTM EPS down 61%). A modest recovery plus a small re-rating gives upside.
JD.risk: Forward EPS may keep getting cut; China market weakness (CSI 300 in a bear market); the Ceconomy bid is a capital-allocation question; analysts cutting targets (Barclays $38, BofA $37).
JD.basis: Fwd EPS $3.63 x 1.05 (1-yr growth +5%) x 8x target P/E

PEGA.thesis: Q3 missed badly (EPS $0.35 vs $0.46; revenue $393M vs $421M) and TTM revenue growth is under 1%. At ~15.6x forward EPS the stock doesn't look cheap enough for that growth.
PEGA.risk: Upside if cloud growth re-accelerates; stock is near the low end of its 52-week range; recent downgrades from JPMorgan and DA Davidson.
PEGA.basis: Fwd EPS $2.34 x 1.08 (1-yr growth +8%) x 15x target P/E

SKHY.thesis: Q3 revenue was 104.6T won with an ~80% operating margin, and HBM demand is booked for more than half of 2027-28 capacity. About 100T won of 2026 shareholder returns is planned. A ~4x forward P/E is normal for peak-cycle memory, so I use a low multiple on flat earnings.
SKHY.risk: Memory is highly cyclical and these margins look like a peak. My price is from Oct 27, before the Q3 report, so the live upside matters. Foreign-ADS structure and currency add risk.
SKHY.basis: Fwd EPS $36.32 x 1.00 (1-yr growth +0%) x 4.5x target P/E

TSLA.thesis: Q3 beat on margin (19.6% gross) and cash flow (~$1.5B), but revenue was flat and net profit fell ~43%. At ~187x forward EPS the price rests on robotaxi, FSD and Optimus options that I can't model.
TSLA.risk: Upside from autonomy and a rumored SpaceX tie-up (Barclays upgrade); downside from an earnings multiple this high if growth disappoints. The energy segment missed badly.
TSLA.basis: Fwd EPS $2.14 x 1.25 (1-yr growth +25%) x 140x target P/E

TTAN.thesis: Software for home-services trades; revenue +23% and a path to profit. The stock dropped ~30% on Sep 9 on growth concerns, and still trades at ~7.6x sales and ~57x forward EPS.
TTAN.risk: Growth issues tied to its AI product, a securities-fraud investigation announcement, and a premium multiple. My model lands just under the return hurdle.
TTAN.basis: Fwd EPS $1.47 x 1.35 (1-yr growth +35%) x 45x target P/E

ZVRA.thesis: Rare-disease drugmaker with revenue +119% and a profit; the stock trades at ~11x forward EPS, and cash ($260M as of Q2) is a large share of the ~$560M market cap.
ZVRA.risk: Concentration in a few products, a negative EU (CHMP) opinion on arimoclomol that cut the stock ~30% in July, and small-cap volatility. Cash figure is from August.
ZVRA.basis: Fwd EPS $0.85 x 1.15 (1-yr growth +15%) x 13x target P/E

IREN.thesis: AI-cloud/bitcoin-mining company with large contracts (reported $9.7B Microsoft deal, $2.8B of new contracts in July) and a >$4B ARR target, but analysts forecast negative EPS for FY27 and I could not retrieve a current quote page, balance sheet, funding plan or the reason for the 2026 drawdown. I would rather not guess a rating.
IREN.risk: Heavy capex and funding needs (dilution/convertible debt), customer concentration, and execution on GPU deployments. Ask me for a deeper pass if you want an opinion.
IREN.basis: No reliable valuation anchor; no price target.
